summary.headline: September was a webinar-driven lead month, but SQLs fell 39% from August and 36% from last September.
summary.body: Web sessions reached 40.3K (+55% YoY) and MQLs rose to 374, led by the Source Material and Lit Talk webinars. MQL to SQL conversion dropped to 20.6% from 44.8%, and SQLs (77) and Opportunities (75) both fell about 39% MoM, which is below the seasonal norm for the back-to-school ramp. HIH reached 110, though 36 came from one Other Campaigns batch. Closed-won was $25.3K, about flat on last September, and MQA accounts stand at 99.

brand_lift.note: These are Google Search numbers, not social engagement — how often our brand and channels surface when people search. YouTube and Instagram are Search Console platform properties, visible in the Search Console UI but not exposed by the Search Analytics API, so those tiles stay blank rather than showing a fabricated zero. LinkedIn has no GSC connector — it's owned by Microsoft and isn't integrated with Google. ⏳ The week of Oct 12 is still provisional: Google has finalized only 5 of its 7 days, so its full-week total (483 branded clicks) is understated and will revise upward on the next run. The WoW figure shown compares the same 5 settled days in each week, which is the like-for-like read; the full-week comparison would be misleading until the week settles.

current.narrative: HIH held steady at 35 (+9% WoW, still Inkwell-led at 30 of 35), while MQL eased slightly to 101 (-9% WoW) but stayed comfortably above its 8-week average (~89). The bigger story is lower-funnel: SQL and Opportunities each roughly doubled WoW to 32, clawing back toward their 8-week averages after two unusually soft weeks, though product tagging on those stages stays thin (under 20% coverage) so the mix is hard to read yet. Disqualified (201) and Nurture (124) both eased further off the W40/W41 list-event spike and no longer trip the list-event thresholds, so that anomaly looks to have fully resolved. Closed-won MTD sits at $417,347, almost entirely from one large renewal (Cherry Creek Schools).

previous.narrative: Oct 5-11: MQL (111), SQL (15) and Opp (16) all cooled off from last week's unusually high totals, though MQL is still running above its 8-week average (~71) even after the pullback. SQL and Opp fell well under their own 8-week averages (~27 each), a signal worth watching for a second week. HIH held at 32 (+14% WoW), with Inkwell (19) again the biggest driver. Disqualified (358) and Nurture (194) eased from last week's flagged spike (868/560) but are still 2.5x+ above normal levels, a second straight week of elevated list activity, still unconfirmed.
